newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Xylan aims at US$1.0 bln revenue by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Xylan aims at US$1.0 bln revenue by 1999.

text.p: Network switching technology company Xylan Corp said on Wednesday it expected to grow several hundred percent and hit revenues of US$1.0 billion by 1999.
Xylan makes local network switching systems it says greatly increase the data available to each desktop computer without having to overhaul the entire network.
"We are saying US$1.0 billion (in revenue) in 1999. We are going to grow several hundred percent this year," president and chief executive officer Steve Kim told reporters.
For the first six months of 1996, Xylan's revenues were $51.6 million and net profits $5.58 million. Its sales in 1995 were about $30 million.
"We think we'll be able to capture 30 to 40 percent of the high end market," Kim said.
According to estimates by Dell'Oro Group, the worldwide LAN (local area network) switching market is expected to grow from $5.03 billion in 1996 to $12.89 billion in 2000.
About 30-40 percent of Xylan's revenue would come from the Asia Pacific region in the long term, Kim said.
